references.text: The same theme that the Father gives the Son life and that the Son gives life to whom He wills, as a direct answer to the question of who has life in Himself.
Reuses the motif that the Son lives because of the Father, and that whoever eats the Son will also live because of Him, which reflects the idea of having life in oneself.
Jesus' prayer confirms that the Father has given the Son authority over all flesh to give eternal life, a direct consequence of the Son having life in Himself.
The foundational connection between the Word and life for eternal life, where life was in the Word, presupposes that the Son has life in Himself.
Jesus' self-identification as the resurrection and the life, and that whoever lives and believes in Him will not die forever, emphasizes that He has life in Himself.
The confirmation that God has given us eternal life, and that this life is in His Son, is a direct parallel to the Father giving the Son life in Himself.
